verses.text: “I made a covenant with my eyes, how then should I look lustfully at a young woman?
lines: “I made a covenant with my eyes,
how then should I look lustfully at a young woman?

verses.text: For what is the portion from God above, and the heritage from the Almighty on high?
lines: For what is the portion from God above,
and the heritage from the Almighty on high?

verses.text: Is it not calamity to the unrighteous, and disaster to the workers of iniquity?
lines: Is it not calamity to the unrighteous,
and disaster to the workers of iniquity?

verses.text: Doesn’t he see my ways, and count all my steps?
lines: Doesn’t he see my ways,
and count all my steps?

verses.text: “If I have walked with falsehood, and my foot has hurried to deceit
lines: “If I have walked with falsehood,
and my foot has hurried to deceit

verses.text: (let me be weighed in an even balance, that God may know my integrity);
lines: (let me be weighed in an even balance,
that God may know my integrity);

verses.text: if my step has turned out of the way, if my heart walked after my eyes, if any defilement has stuck to my hands,
lines: if my step has turned out of the way,
if my heart walked after my eyes,
if any defilement has stuck to my hands,

verses.text: then let me sow, and let another eat. Yes, let the produce of my field be rooted out.
lines: then let me sow, and let another eat.
Yes, let the produce of my field be rooted out.

verses.text: “If my heart has been enticed to a woman, and I have laid wait at my neighbor’s door,
lines: “If my heart has been enticed to a woman,
and I have laid wait at my neighbor’s door,

verses.text: then let my wife grind for another, and let others sleep with her.
lines: then let my wife grind for another,
and let others sleep with her.

verses.text: For that would be a heinous crime. Yes, it would be an iniquity to be punished by the judges;
lines: For that would be a heinous crime.
Yes, it would be an iniquity to be punished by the judges;

verses.text: for it is a fire that consumes to destruction, and would root out all my increase.
lines: for it is a fire that consumes to destruction,
and would root out all my increase.

verses.text: “If I have despised the cause of my male servant or of my female servant, when they contended with me,
lines: “If I have despised the cause of my male servant
or of my female servant,
when they contended with me,

verses.text: what then will I do when God rises up? When he visits, what will I answer him?
lines: what then will I do when God rises up?
When he visits, what will I answer him?

verses.text: Didn’t he who made me in the womb make him? Didn’t one fashion us in the womb?
lines: Didn’t he who made me in the womb make him?
Didn’t one fashion us in the womb?

verses.text: “If I have withheld the poor from their desire, or have caused the eyes of the widow to fail,
lines: “If I have withheld the poor from their desire,
or have caused the eyes of the widow to fail,

verses.text: or have eaten my morsel alone, and the fatherless has not eaten of it
lines: or have eaten my morsel alone,
and the fatherless has not eaten of it

verses.text: (no, from my youth he grew up with me as with a father, I have guided her from my mother’s womb);
lines: (no, from my youth he grew up with me as with a father,
I have guided her from my mother’s womb);

verses.text: if I have seen any perish for want of clothing, or that the needy had no covering;
lines: if I have seen any perish for want of clothing,
or that the needy had no covering;

verses.text: if his heart hasn’t blessed me, if he hasn’t been warmed with my sheep’s fleece;
lines: if his heart hasn’t blessed me,
if he hasn’t been warmed with my sheep’s fleece;

verses.text: if I have lifted up my hand against the fatherless, because I saw my help in the gate,
lines: if I have lifted up my hand against the fatherless,
because I saw my help in the gate,

verses.text: then let my shoulder fall from the shoulder blade, and my arm be broken from the bone.
lines: then let my shoulder fall from the shoulder blade,
and my arm be broken from the bone.

verses.text: For calamity from God is a terror to me. Because of his majesty, I can do nothing.
lines: For calamity from God is a terror to me.
Because of his majesty, I can do nothing.

verses.text: “If I have made gold my hope, and have said to the fine gold, ‘You are my confidence;’
lines: “If I have made gold my hope,
and have said to the fine gold, ‘You are my confidence;’

verses.text: If I have rejoiced because my wealth was great, and because my hand had gotten much;
lines: If I have rejoiced because my wealth was great,
and because my hand had gotten much;

verses.text: if I have seen the sun when it shined, or the moon moving in splendor,
lines: if I have seen the sun when it shined,
or the moon moving in splendor,

verses.text: and my heart has been secretly enticed, and my hand threw a kiss from my mouth,
lines: and my heart has been secretly enticed,
and my hand threw a kiss from my mouth,

verses.text: this also would be an iniquity to be punished by the judges; for I should have denied the God who is above.
lines: this also would be an iniquity to be punished by the judges;
for I should have denied the God who is above.

verses.text: “If I have rejoiced at the destruction of him who hated me, or lifted up myself when evil found him
lines: “If I have rejoiced at the destruction of him who hated me,
or lifted up myself when evil found him

verses.text: (yes, I have not allowed my mouth to sin by asking his life with a curse);
lines: (yes, I have not allowed my mouth to sin
by asking his life with a curse);

verses.text: if the men of my tent have not said, ‘Who can find one who has not been filled with his meat?’
lines: if the men of my tent have not said,
‘Who can find one who has not been filled with his meat?’

verses.text: (the foreigner has not camped in the street, but I have opened my doors to the traveler);
lines: (the foreigner has not camped in the street,
but I have opened my doors to the traveler);

verses.text: if like Adam I have covered my transgressions, by hiding my iniquity in my heart,
lines: if like Adam I have covered my transgressions,
by hiding my iniquity in my heart,

verses.text: because I feared the great multitude, and the contempt of families terrified me, so that I kept silence, and didn’t go out of the door—
lines: because I feared the great multitude,
and the contempt of families terrified me,
so that I kept silence, and didn’t go out of the door—

verses.text: oh that I had one to hear me! Behold, here is my signature! Let the Almighty answer me! Let the accuser write my indictment!
lines: oh that I had one to hear me!
Behold, here is my signature! Let the Almighty answer me!
Let the accuser write my indictment!

verses.text: Surely I would carry it on my shoulder; and I would bind it to me as a crown.
lines: Surely I would carry it on my shoulder;
and I would bind it to me as a crown.

verses.text: I would declare to him the number of my steps. as a prince would I go near to him.
lines: I would declare to him the number of my steps.
as a prince would I go near to him.

verses.text: If my land cries out against me, and its furrows weep together;
lines: If my land cries out against me,
and its furrows weep together;
